confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-ter (EC-6): `declare function resolveInteractive(env, ref): InteractiveElement;` and `nameSourceOf`, commented "DECLARED BY THIS CONTRACT. Total over InteractiveRef. Never throws, never returns undefined" and "total by type over the closed six-member union — no default branch is reachable"; with A-2's mechanism reading `a11y.accessible_names[refKey(ref)].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref, env).label)`.
confirmedFindings.justification:
Both halves survive verification against the declaring shapes, and neither is covered by §0.16, §0B.9 or §0C.13.

(a) STRATEGY_OPTIONS — the decisive half. §2.6.11 declares `alternatives: Array<{ option_id: string; title: Cell<string>; reasoning: NarrativeText; expected_effect: Measure; risk_tier; reversible: Cell<boolean>; audience_size: Measure | null; select_intent: string }>` — there is NO `label` member — and §2.6.11's "**Interactive paths** `alternatives[].option_id`, `no_action_option.select_intent`" means an `{k:'option'}` ref on a STRATEGY_OPTIONS envelope denotes exactly that shape. §0C.22-ter's `InteractiveElement` union is `WidgetIntent | FormField | OptionItem | ReportBody['sections'][number] | ScheduleBody['entries'][number] | { table; row }` — it names no StrategyOptions-alternative branch, so `resolveInteractive`, declared to RETURN `InteractiveElement`, cannot return the element this ref denotes; and `nameSourceOf`'s `case 'option': return { label: el.label.label, from: 'option' }` reads `.label` on a shape that declares none, yielding `undefined` and then throwing on the second access — precisely what the same paragraph says it never does. §0C.22-ter's supporting prose makes the wrong assumption explicit: "`OptionItem.label`, `entries[].title` and a table row's header cell are all `Cell<T>`" — it assumes every `option` ref denotes an `OptionItem`. §2.6.2 and §2.6.3 type their options `Array<OptionItem & { … }>` for exactly this reason; §2.6.11 does not. §0.16 E-24/E-25/E-26 amend `reversible`, `expected_effect` and the shape's provenance, and retype nothing.

(b) TIME_SLOT_SELECTOR. §2.6.4 declares "**Interactive paths** `groups[].slots[].slot_ref`, `more_intent`, `widen_window_intent`, `none_fit_intent`" over `slots: Array<{ slot_ref: string; start: Measure; duration: Measure; staff_ref; price; availability; intent_token }>`. §4.8's `InteractiveRef` is a closed six-member union — `option`, `field`, `intent`, `row`, `entry`, `section` — with no member for a slot (verified: zero occurrences of a `slot` member anywhere in the file). A slot is not an `OptionItem` either: §0.29 enumerates "`OptionItem.intent_token`, `slots[].intent_token`" as DISTINCT repeated-element handles. EC-17 (§0C.28-bis) makes `interactive_paths` the sole authority on per-kind membership and K22's mechanism "recomputes the ref set from `interactive_paths` and refuses on any difference" — but EC-17 verified only one direction ("no kind's `interactive_paths` names a `series_id`"), never the converse, that every produced path maps to a declared member. Its stated ground for excluding `series_id` — §1.2's **structural** class — does not distinguish it: `option_id`, `intent_token`, `slot_ref`, `section_id`, `field_key` are all in that same list.

Consequence in both cases is fail-closed (a refused mint / a build that cannot be written), so no forbidden edge becomes constructible — but the sentence asserting the mechanism is total, non-throwing and never-undefined is not true of the shapes the contract actually declares, and A-2's CI check cannot be written against them. This is the exact defect class §0C.22-ter was written to close ("only `{k: 'intent'}` denotes a `WidgetIntent`"), reproduced one shape further in.
confirmedFindings.repair: Two edits, both inside §0C.22-ter. (1) Retype §2.6.11's alternatives as `Array<OptionItem & { reasoning: NarrativeText; expected_effect: Measure | null; risk_tier; reversible: Cell<boolean>; audience_size: Measure | null; select_intent: string }>` — following §2.6.2 and §2.6.3 verbatim — so the single `case 'option'` branch is sound for all four option-producing kinds, and state that `title` is subsumed by `OptionItem.label`. (2) Add a seventh member `{ k: 'slot'; id: string }` to `InteractiveRef`, a matching `TimeSlotSelectorBody['groups'][number]['slots'][number]` branch to `InteractiveElement`, and `case 'slot': return { label: el.start.label, from: 'slot' }` to `nameSourceOf`; restate `refKey`'s injectivity over seven fixed tokens rather than six, and amend §0C.22-ter's "closed six-member union" wording and EC-6's errata row to seven. (A-6's "Eleven slots are one tab stop, not eleven" and §4.8.2's TIME_SLOT_SELECTOR keyboard model both presuppose per-slot reading-order members, so deleting the path instead is not open.)

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-quinquies (EC-6): "**the other seventeen carry the declared default `''`** (the empty suffix), for which A-2's composition reduces to `nameSourceOf(ref, env).label` verbatim — so the rule is total over all twenty-two kinds with no 'otherwise' branch left to interpretation", enforced by A-2's "and, for every kind §4.8.2 names, **equality** with the row's composition applied to the emitted body".
confirmedFindings.justification:
Quoted and verified at the artefact: §4.8.2's SERVICE_SELECTOR row, text-alternative column — "each option's duration and price **in the accessible name**"; STAFF_SELECTOR — "`nearest_availability` **in the accessible name**"; STRATEGY_OPTIONS, non-colour-state column — "`recommended` is a text token **in the accessible name** and **never a pre-selection**"; CLIENT_LIST, keyboard-model column — "A-17; row intents are in-row buttons; bulk intents outside the table", and §4.8.1 A-17 reads "Bulk intents sit outside the table and carry `audience_size` **in the accessible name**." All four columns are expressly preserved: §0B.35 voids only the `role_hint` column and states "its keyboard-model, text-alternative, live-region and non-colour-state columns stand", and EB-12 repeats "The other four columns stand." Nothing downgrades them — §0.17 item 1 downgrades §2.5's twelve-row table, not §4.8.1's clauses; §0C.12 lists three items, none of them these; no row of §0.16, §0B.9 or §0C.13 touches them (EC-6's row voids only `intent.utterance`).

The conflict is exact. Under `accessible_name_suffix = ''` A-2's composition reduces to `nameSourceOf(ref, env).label` verbatim, and A-2's mechanism asserts EQUALITY (not containment) "for every kind §4.8.2 names" — which, after EB-13 amended the table to twenty-two, is every kind. The source values those rows demand are separate declared members, not part of the label: §2.6.2 types the option as `OptionItem & { duration: Measure; price: Measure; … }`; §2.6.3 as `OptionItem & { nearest_availability: Measure; … }`; §2.6.7 as `bulk_intents: Array<{ intent_token; label; audience_size: Measure }>` whose ref is `{k:'intent'}`, so `nameSourceOf` returns the bare `intent.label`. So an emission that carries duration, price, `nearest_availability` or `audience_size` in the accessible name FAILS the very CI check A-2 names, and one that omits them violates the row's own surviving column. Two same-precedence clauses that cannot both be satisfied; "total … with no 'otherwise' branch left to interpretation" is untrue of these rows. The drafter's own treatment of APPROVAL settles the intended rule against them: APPROVAL's accessible-name prose lives in §4.8.2's keyboard-model column, not in §0B.36, and §0C.22-quinquies nevertheless populates its suffix (`audience_size`, `risk_tier`, reversibility) — the identical basis exists for these four and was not applied. Recorded caveat: `recommended` occurs exactly once in the whole artefact (that row) and `StrategyOptionsBody` declares no such member, so that row's phrase has no artefact to compose from and is the weakest of the four; SERVICE_SELECTOR, STAFF_SELECTOR and CLIENT_LIST are load-bearing, and CLIENT_LIST additionally removes the one disclosure A-17 exists for, which §2.6.7 CLIENT.1 and K9's `audience`-before-`options` ordering treat as required before the control is reachable.
confirmedFindings.repair: Populate `accessible_name_suffix` for those rows from their own surviving columns rather than leaving them `''` — SERVICE_SELECTOR: `duration`, `price`; STAFF_SELECTOR: `nearest_availability`; CLIENT_LIST: `audience_size` on `bulk_intents[]` — and restate §0C.22-quinquies's tally as eight populated rows and fourteen carrying the declared empty default. For STRATEGY_OPTIONS, either declare the `recommended` member on `StrategyOptionsBody['alternatives'][number]` and populate the suffix from it, or void that phrase of §4.8.2's non-colour-state column explicitly in §0C.13; silence on which of the two columns governs is the one outcome the bar does not permit.

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.28-ter (EC-11): "An envelope whose `capability.space` is 'C9' and whose `correlation.agent_id` is null is REFUSED at `EP-MINT`: there is no second source and none is invented." / "A `C9` intent minted with `c9_domain === null` is refused at `EP-MINT`, and so is one whose envelope carries `correlation.agent_id === null`."
confirmedFindings.justification:
Re-read at artefact lines 2378-2403 and cross-checked against §1.1.4 (line 2787), §1.1.2 (line 2756), §0.16 E-29 (line 471), §4.1.1 L1 (line 5224) and §0C.11(5) (lines 1499-1518). Verified in process: C9Domain is exactly the four run-agent domains (c9.contract.ts:5-11) and c9Capability's `domain` is a required positional argument (c9.registry.ts:178-192). An exhaustive grep of the artefact finds `Correlation.agent_id` (line 2787) as the SINGLE domain-valued member — so §0C.28-ter's own premise ("there is no second source") is true, which is exactly what makes the refusal bite.

The chain is closed and unsatisfiable on one of two declared mint paths: (1) §1.1.4 declares `run_id` nullable "because two paths mint envelopes: a coordination run … and a registered capability read", and §4.1.1 L1 names "a registered capability read endpoint" as minter (2) of three. (2) §0.16 E-29 fixes `agent_id` as class D "derived by the minter from the run's registered agent". On a run-less capability read there is no registered agent. (3) §1.1.2 gives the composer only `correlation_refs: // run/turn/message/parent ids only` — no `agent_id` member — so no composer-side source exists either, and §0C.28-ter expressly forbids the one remaining candidate ("NEVER from the subject capability's own `domains`"). Therefore `correlation.agent_id` is null by construction on that path, and every envelope carrying a `capability.space === 'C9'` intent is refused at EP-MINT.

§0.32/§0B.7 put every `REFINE` and every `DRAFT` in the C9 space (`HANDOFF` is not caught: its `capability` is null, so `capability.space` is not 'C9', and `c9_domain` is correctly null by the declared IFF). The refused population is therefore every REFINE- or DRAFT-bearing envelope minted from a capability read, including intents the bodies declare mandatory and non-nullable: §2.6.4 `none_fit_intent: string` ("REFINE — always present, never droppable") over `booking.availability.read`; §2.6.2/§2.6.3 selector DRAFTs over `catalog.services.read`/`catalog.staff.read`; §2.6.8 `compare_intent`/`drill_intent` over `c7.measurement.read`; §0.36's `SCHEDULE.entries[].move_intent` over `appointments.own.reschedule`; CLIENT_LIST's `b35.preview`/`b35.status` REFINEs; `ARTIFACT.regenerate_intent` over `owner_report.download`.

That is an intra-section conflict of equal precedence, not a cross-section one resolved by precedence: §0C.11(5) states "the five kinds §0C.9 named become emittable", and four of §0C.9's named casualties — CLIENT_LIST, METRIC, CHART, ARTIFACT — are exactly the capability-read-sourced kinds EC-11 now refuses. §0C.9 itself ranks this precise shape ("`STRATEGY_OPTIONS` is unemittable, contradicting §0.40's seventeen") as the section's first-ranked structural defect; EC-11 reproduces it one erratum later by a different route. The failure is fail-closed, and §0C.32's "No repair admits a capability, widens an allowlist, or relaxes a veto" survives — but the section nowhere discloses that a repair removes a declared first-class mint path, and §2.6.4's non-nullable `none_fit_intent` becomes an unsatisfiable requirement there. The repair is not INERT and not a misreading: the refusal is stated twice, unscoped, and its sole antecedent is provably null on that path.
confirmedFindings.repair: Scope the refusal to the path on which its antecedent can be evaluated. Replace §0C.28-ter's two refusal sentences with: "An envelope whose `correlation.run_id !== null` and which carries an intent with `capability.space === 'C9'` is REFUSED at `EP-MINT` when `correlation.agent_id` is null. On the run-less registered-capability-read path (§1.1.4, §4.1.1 L1 minter 2) `c9_domain` is null by construction, and EC-11's second Gate 6 `C9` branch there reduces to `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY[capKey(ref)]` must exist (else refuse) plus `CONSENT_CLASS_FLOOR` carried through `c9Floor` at Gate 5 — the `c9Capability` domain half is explicitly NOT applied on that path, and this contract says so rather than leaving a gate that cannot call its own fence." Amend §0C.28-bis's Gate 6 pseudocode identically (the `record.c9_domain` argument is only reachable when `record.run_ref !== null`), and add the resulting reduction to §0C.32's disclosure table alongside the two floor reductions, since the nine non-catalogue keys then keep only their policy-row and consent-class fence on that path — which §0C.28-bis already states is the real fence for them. (Alternative, larger repair: declare a widget-layer `WIDGET_READ_DOMAIN: Readonly<Record<OwnerClass, C9Domain>>`, mint class D, asserted at `EP-REGISTRY-LOAD` against `c9Registry.tryGet(key).domains` for every key each owner class resolves; this is a widget-layer table, so `C9_REGISTRY_HASH` and FR-16 are untouched.)
